evidence: Dry run on a fresh copy of the base snapshot: `git apply --check -v patch.diff` reported 'Checking patch' for docs/source/transforms.rst, monai/transforms/utility/array.py, monai/transforms/utility/dictionary.py, tests/test_lambda.py, tests/test_lambdad.py with no errors.
checks.json: patch_applies=true, commands=[] (no tests run, per instruction).

diff -rq base vs generated: only the 3 patched files plus the 2 new test files differ; the `.git` entry in generated also appears in the reference tree, so it is a harness artifact, not a candidate change.

Caveat (not a patch failure): candidate test methods are named test_identity/test_slicing (tests/test_lambda.py:21,26; tests/test_lambdad.py:21,28), while prepared.json lists FAIL_TO_PASS IDs test_lambda_identity/test_lambda_slicing/test_lambdad_identity/test_lambdad_slicing. If the candidate test files are kept instead of replaced by the official ones, those IDs would not be found.
Lambda class placed at the end of monai/transforms/utility/array.py:296-322, same module and position as reference array.py.
Lambdad placed in monai/transforms/utility/dictionary.py:417-449 next to the other dictionary transforms, same as reference dictionary.py:417.
Docs entries at docs/source/transforms.rst:346-349 (Vanilla Transforms) and :704-707 (Dictionary-based Transforms), matching the reference locations.
Tests at tests/test_lambda.py and tests/test_lambdad.py, matching reference paths.

Lambda.__init__(self, func: Callable) at monai/transforms/utility/array.py:313 with assert callable(func) at :318; __call__(self, img) at :321 returns self.func(img) at :322. Matches reference array.py Lambda.

Lambdad.__init__(self, keys: KeysCollection, func: Callable) at monai/transforms/utility/dictionary.py:434; __call__(self, data) at ~:445. Matches reference dictionary.py:437 signature (reference adds '-> None'; base classes such as CopyItemsd omit it, so the patch follows base convention).
Alias LambdaD = LambdaDict = Lambdad at dictionary.py:465, same as reference.
dictionary.py:39 imports Lambda from monai.transforms.utility.array, the same direction as the existing imports of array transforms in dictionary.py (base dictionary.py:21-40).
array.py is unchanged in its imports; the only import change is dictionary.py:19 `from typing import Callable, Optional`, which adds a stdlib name to an existing line.
No new module dependency is introduced in the dictionary -> array direction.

monai/transforms/__init__.py:21-22 star-imports utility.array and utility.dictionary; grep for __all__ across monai/transforms returned nothing, so Lambda and Lambdad are exported without further registration (same as reference).
Dictionary alias LambdaD/LambdaDict registered at dictionary.py:465.
Docs registration via autoclass at docs/source/transforms.rst:346-349 and :704-707.
No new third-party dependency. The only new name is typing.Callable (dictionary.py:19), which array.py already imports from typing at line 14.
Test files use only numpy, unittest and the existing tests.utils.NumpyImageTestCase2D (tests/test_lambda.py:14-20).

Array-level logic lives in the array module (array.py:296-322) and the dictionary wrapper delegates to it: self.lambd = Lambda(func) at dictionary.py:443. This matches the reference structure (reference dictionary.py:439).
No logic is duplicated between Lambda and Lambdad.
Lambda subclasses Transform (array.py:296), the existing base for array transforms.
Lambdad subclasses MapTransform and calls super().__init__(keys) (dictionary.py:417, 434-443), the existing base for dictionary transforms.
Alias naming follows the existing pattern (dictionary.py:458-465, e.g. IdentityD = IdentityDict = Identityd).
Lambdad copies the input dict before writing (dictionary.py:446 `d = dict(data)`), matching existing dictionary transforms such as ConcatItemsd and CopyItemsd in base dictionary.py.
Only the keys in self.keys are touched (dictionary.py:447-448); the transform does not mutate the caller's dict.
Validation uses assert callable(func) with message 'func must be callable' (array.py:318), the same as reference array.py.
Docstrings use Args: sections and runnable Example code blocks, consistent with existing transforms (dictionary.py Lambdad docstring 417-433).
Tests follow the repo pattern: license header, unittest.TestCase subclass of NumpyImageTestCase2D (tests/test_lambda.py:20, tests/test_lambdad.py:20), and a __main__ guard.
Test method names (test_identity, test_slicing) differ from reference (test_lambda_identity, etc.). This is a naming difference, not a repo convention violation.
Lambda applies the user callable to the whole input and returns its result (array.py:321-322), as the reference does.
Lambdad applies the callable to each listed key on a shallow copy and leaves other keys unchanged (dictionary.py:446-449), as the reference does.
Non-callable func is rejected at construction via assert (array.py:318; dictionary.py via Lambda(func) at :443).
Docstring examples are correct: x[:, 1:] applied to shape (1, 3, 4) gives shape (1, 2, 4) (array.py:296-310 example; dictionary.py:417-433 example).
Diff against base is additions only (plus the typing import line), so there are no regressions.
